question.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡z)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡z)\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡z)\,k \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡z}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡z}\,i-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡z}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡z}\,j+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\operatorname{cos}⁡z}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡z}\,k \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡x\,i-\operatorname{tan}⁡y\,j+\operatorname{cot}⁡z\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=t,$ $y={t}^{2}$ and $z={e}^{t}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\operatorname{cot}⁡t\,i-\operatorname{tan}⁡{t}^{2}\,j+\operatorname{cot}⁡{e}^{t}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,k \\  & =i+2t\,j+{e}^{t}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\operatorname{cot}⁡t\,i-\operatorname{tan}⁡{t}^{2}\,j+\operatorname{cot}⁡{e}^{t}\,k)\cdot (i+2t\,j+{e}^{t}\,k) \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡t-2t\operatorname{tan}⁡{t}^{2}+{e}^{t}\operatorname{cot}⁡{e}^{t}.\end{aligned}
$$
